---
title: "Caching"
description: "Cache layers, keys, trust model, miss debugging, and cost bounds for builds, tests, type checks, and CI."
updatedAt: "2026-10-23"
---

Caching makes unchanged work skip. It must never replay a pass for inputs that
changed. This page covers build and validation caching only. Product runtime
caching (Next `use cache`, cache tags, CDN or KV) has tenant-isolation rules of
its own and is out of scope here.

## Cache layers

| Layer | Where it lives | Key | Who may write |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Turbo local cache | `.turbo/cache` per checkout, or `TURBO_CACHE_DIR` | Turbo task hash | Any local run |
| Turbo remote cache | Vercel today; self-hosted Cloudflare R2 Worker planned | Turbo task hash, team-scoped | Trusted `main`/`production` jobs and trusted machines |
| Turbo fallback archive | GitHub Actions cache (`setup-turbo-fallback-cache`) | OS + arch + family + `turbo.json` + `bun.lock` + SHA | Default-branch jobs only |
| Bun runtime and packages | GitHub Actions cache (`setup-bun-with-retry`) | Bun version + `bun.lock` | Trusted `main` only |
| Supabase images and baseline | GitHub Actions cache (`cache-supabase-images`, `setup-supabase-baseline`) | Image pins / migration fingerprint | Trusted `main` only |
| Tool incremental state | `*.tsbuildinfo`, `.turbo/tsc-build-cache-key.json` | Stored as Turbo outputs | Follows the Turbo cache |
| Mobile toolchains | Flutter SDK, pub, Gradle, CocoaPods caches | Toolchain version + lockfiles | Today also pull-request refs; must move to `main` only |

The Turbo cache is the only layer that replaces work. Every other layer only
saves downloads. Restoring an archive is not a task hit: Turbo still verifies
each task hash. Read `Cached: N cached, M total` in the run output for actual
reuse.

## How Turbo decides a hit

A task hash combines a global hash and a task hash.

- **Global hash:** `.gitattributes`, the root package's external dependencies,
  the root package's **workspace dependency closure**, `globalEnv` values,
  `globalPassThroughEnv` names, and the root `turbo.json` definition. A change
  to any of these invalidates every task.
- **Task hash:** the task's resolved `inputs` (default: git-tracked files in the
  package), its external dependency hash from `bun.lock`, its `env` values, and
  the hashes of every task it `dependsOn`.

Dependency hashes are what keep caching correct. `type-check` depends on
`^build` and `^type-check`, and `test` depends on `transit`, which depends on
`^transit`. A source edit in `packages/utils` therefore invalidates every
dependent type check and test. Do not narrow these links. In particular, do
not exclude upstream `__tests__` folders from them:
`apps/web/src/app/api/v1/sso/routes.test.ts` imports
`packages/sso/src/__tests__/fixture` by relative path.

## Invariants

`scripts/ci/turbo-cache-config.test.js` enforces these rules:

1. **No root runtime workspace dependencies.** A root
   `"@tuturuuu/email-service": "workspace:*"` dependency put email-service,
   utils, types, internal-api and supabase into the global hash, so any edit to
   them invalidated every task. Root scripts that need a workspace package
   import its source path instead (see the Docker watcher in
   `scripts/watch-blue-green/incident-email.js`). The only allowed root
   workspace link is the `@tuturuuu/typescript-config` dev dependency, which
   legitimately affects every type check.
2. **No volatile or machine-specific hashed env.** Never hash run IDs, SHAs,
   timestamps, `GITHUB_*`/`RUNNER_*`, or machine paths (`PUB_CACHE`,
   `LOCALAPPDATA`, `USERPROFILE`). Put machine paths in
   `globalPassThroughEnv`. Only deploy builds hash `PLATFORM_BUILD_*`, because
   the emitted app embeds that identity. `globalEnv` still hashes runtime
   secrets such as `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` into every
   task, so a shell that exports them gets no hits from CI. Keep them in
   app `.env` files, not the shell profile. Moving them to task env does not
   help today, because no-script placeholder `build` tasks would still carry
   them into every type-check hash.
3. **No remote-cache credentials in any env list.** `TURBO_TOKEN`, `TURBO_TEAM`,
   `TURBO_API` and `TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY` stay step-scoped (see
   `ci-cache-policy.test.js`).
4. **Caching is opt-out only for an allowlist:** `dev`, persistent `serve:*`
   tasks, `test:watch`, `test:e2e`, and the runtime browser suite. Every other
   task declares `outputs`; check-only tasks use `[]`.
5. **Narrowed `inputs` keep `$TURBO_DEFAULT$`.** Package `turbo.json` files
   extend `//` and add to inherited inputs with `$TURBO_EXTENDS$`.
6. **Gitignored files that change results are hashed.** `test` hashes `.env*`
   because Vitest configs call `loadEnv(process.cwd())`. Packages whose type
   check runs `wrangler types` or `cf workers types` hash `.dev.vars*` and
   `.env*`, and cache the generated declarations their tsconfig reads
   (`worker-configuration.d.ts` or `.cloudflare/types/**`) so a cache hit on
   a fresh checkout restores them.
7. **The local cache is bounded:** `cacheMaxAge: "7d"` and
   `cacheMaxSize: "4GB"`. These settings do not change task hashes.

## Measured effect

A dry-run replay (`turbo run <task> --dry=json`, no task executed) of 40
consecutive first-parent `main` commits on 2026-10-23 measured the share of
task hashes that already existed at the parent commit. That share is the hit
rate a perfectly warm cache seeded by the PR base would give.

| Configuration | type-check | test | build | Commits that miss every task |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before (root email-service dependency) | 64.8% | 64.0% | 64.0% | 11 of 40 |
| After | 70.3% | 69.2% | 69.2% | 4 of 40 |

The remaining full misses are dependency upgrades and edits to `turbo.json`
env lists. Both are legitimate global changes. Most other misses are correct
cascades from shared packages.

The replay is an upper bound. Real CI only reaches it when a warm cache is
available. In the same week the repository's Actions cache was at its 10 GB
limit. Pull-request-scoped Flutter SDK (1.6–2.1 GB each) and Gradle (3.6 GB)
entries evicted the default-branch Turbo fallback and Supabase image archives,
so branch type checks logged `Cache not found` and ran cold. Mobile toolchain
caches must restore on pull requests and save only from `main`, like the Bun
and Supabase caches already do.

## Trust model

- Pull requests, forks and Dependabot get no Turbo remote-cache credentials.
  They restore only default-branch Actions caches and never save them, which
  prevents cache poisoning.
- Trusted `main` and `production` jobs read and write the remote cache.
- The planned self-hosted cache adds signed artifacts
  (`TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY`) and read-only tokens for untrusted
  contexts. Its runbook covers cutover, rollback and cost. Until cutover, the
  Vercel-backed cache stays the fallback.
- Local machines use remote credentials only from the user's shell profile or
  secret store. Never commit them or write them to `.env` files that Turbo
  hashes.

## Debug a miss

1. Compute hashes without running anything:

   ```bash
   bun turbo:local run type-check --filter=@tuturuuu/utils --dry=json > /tmp/a.json
   ```

2. Repeat on the comparison commit, or in the CI environment, then compare
   `globalCacheInputs`. If `hashOfInternalDependencies` differs, a root
   workspace dependency changed. If `environmentVariables` differs, a hashed
   env value differs between the two runs.
3. For one task, compare `inputs` (file to git hash),
   `hashOfExternalDependencies`, `environmentVariables.configured`, and the
   hashes of the tasks listed in `dependencies`. The first differing component
   is the cause.
4. In CI, read the run logs. `cache miss, executing <hash>` versus
   `cache hit, replaying logs <hash>` gives per-task results. The
   **Turbo fallback archive** step summary shows whether the archive restored
   at all.
5. `--summarize` writes `.turbo/runs/<id>.json` with each task's
   `cache.status`, `local`/`remote` source, and `timeSaved`.

## Run only what changed

Combine affected selection with a warm cache. Unchanged dependency tasks
replay from the cache, and only the changed packages and their dependents
execute.

```bash
TURBO_SCM_BASE=origin/main bun turbo:local run test type-check --affected
bun turbo:local run test --filter='...[origin/main]'
```

Both select the packages changed since the base plus their dependents. Turbo
still schedules their dependency tasks, which are cache hits when nothing
upstream changed. An edit to a root file (`turbo.json`, root `package.json`,
`bun.lock` root entries, `.gitattributes`) selects everything; that is
expected. For a single package, a package-local command such as
`bun --cwd packages/ai vitest run <file>` avoids Turbo entirely. Queue broad
runs with `ttr resources run -- <command>`.

### Share the local cache across worktrees

Each worktree has its own `.turbo/cache` by default. Trusted machines can share
one bounded cache across worktrees by exporting an absolute path in the shell
profile:

```bash
export TURBO_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/.cache/turbo/tuturuuu"
```

Turbo does not coordinate concurrent writers. Entries are keyed by task hash,
so two worktrees racing on one hash write the same artifact. If a restore ever
fails, delete that hash's files from the directory and rerun. The `cacheMaxAge`
and `cacheMaxSize` bounds apply to the shared directory. Do not set
`TURBO_CACHE_DIR` in CI: the fallback archive action expects `.turbo/cache`.

## Cost bounds

- GitHub Actions cache: 10 GB per repository with least-recently-used
  eviction. Save only from `main`, keep keys stable, and do not let
  pull-request refs create multi-GB entries.
- Local Turbo cache: 7 days and 4 GB per cache directory.
- Remote cache: request, size, TTL and operation-count bounds for the
  self-hosted Worker are defined in its runbook.
